title: Missing 2π? Dimensional Limits Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A ruler cannot read colour. A thermometer cannot read your mood. Every tool has a limit, and so does dimensional analysis. Aarav used it to find how the corridor swing's time depends on length and g, but the textbook formula has a 2π his method could never find. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we see exactly what dimensional analysis cannot do, and why.

A live pendulum on the measuring bench swings at 0.5 m, 1 m and 2 m while the readout divides T by √(l/g) and gets 6.28 every time, and the graph shows a straight line with slope 2π. We let the method derive T = k√(l/g) step by step, then follow the reasoning link by link: k is a plain number with dimensions M⁰L⁰T⁰, so dimensions can never choose its value. Two pause-and-think questions test a fake formula with balanced dimensions and work vs torque. Then sums, sine, log and the three-equation limit, a worked example that finds k = 2π by measuring, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
